requirementDefs.doc:
A regulatory, legal, or standards obligation that
the business must satisfy. General vocabulary —
applicable to COSHH, CQC, GDPR, food hygiene,
professional standards, or any regulatory context.
Domain-specific requirement usages redefine these
attributes with concrete values. The satisfy chain

userFacing.shortDescription: A regulatory or standards obligation that the business must satisfy, with defined evidence.

purposiveDescription.description: A regulatory, legal, or standards obligation that your business must satisfy — and the system tracks it as a concrete, testable commitment, not just a policy statement. Each governance requirement is connected to the evidence that demonstrates compliance and, where formalised, to the constraint rules that the system can check. When you define governance requirements, the system builds a traceability chain from obligation through to proof.

requirementDefs.name: ConsentBeforeTreatment
requirementDefs.doc:
Informed consent must be obtained and recorded
before any treatment is initiated. Consent must
be specific to the proposed treatment, documented
in the clinical record, and include evidence that
the patient had capacity at the time of consent.
Regulatory basis: GMC Good Medical Practice,
Montgomery

requirementDefs.name: InformedConsentRequiresInformation
requirementDefs.doc:
Before consent can be considered informed, the patient
must have received and had opportunity to consider
relevant information about the proposed treatment,
including expected effects, potential risks, alternative
options, and the consequences of not proceeding.

requirementDefs.name: BaselineInvestigationsBeforePrescribing
requirementDefs.doc:
Baseline blood tests must be completed, resulted,
and reviewed by a clinician before a hormone therapy
prescription is authorised. The required baseline
panel includes FBC, U&Es, LFTs, lipid profile,
fasting glucose, prolactin, and baseline hormone
levels (testosterone, oestradiol).

requirementDefs.name: ClinicalReviewBeforePrescribing
requirementDefs.doc:
A clinician with appropriate competence must conduct
a clinical review before authorising a hormone therapy
prescription. The review must consider baseline
investigations, patient history, contraindications,
and the proposed regimen.
This applies to both initial prescribing and any
subsequent dose a

requirementDefs.name: PrescribingProtocolAdherence
requirementDefs.doc:
Prescribing must follow an approved clinical protocol.
The protocol defines eligible medications, routes of
administration, starting doses, titration schedules,
and therapeutic target ranges.
Deviations from protocol must be clinically justified
and documented in the clinical record.

requirementDefs.name: BloodMonitoringRequired
requirementDefs.doc:
Patients on hormone therapy must have blood tests
performed at defined monitoring intervals. The
monitoring schedule is determined by the prescribing
protocol and the patient's clinical stability.
Initial monitoring is typically at 3 months post-
initiation, then at intervals determined by clinical

requirementDefs.name: ClinicalReviewBeforeDoseAdjustment
requirementDefs.doc:
Any change to hormone therapy dosage must be preceded
by a clinical review that considers current blood
results, symptom assessment, side effect evaluation,
and the patient's overall clinical picture.
Dose adjustments without clinical review are not
permitted, even when blood results suggest a chang

requirementDefs.name: SharedCareCommunication
requirementDefs.doc:
When hormone therapy monitoring is transitioned to
shared care with the patient's GP, the GP must receive
a shared care protocol document that includes the
current regimen, monitoring schedule, therapeutic
target ranges, action thresholds, and clear guidance
on when to refer back.

requirementDefs.doc:
Members of the loyalty scheme must receive
a minimum 10% discount on every order.

requirementDefs.name: MinimumOrderSize
requirementDefs.doc: Orders must contain at least one item.

requirementDefs.name: MaximumOrderSize
requirementDefs.doc:
Orders must contain no more than 10 items
to avoid barista overload.

requirementDefs.name: veganMilkDrinkRule
requirementDefs.doc:
Any drink marked as vegan must not use
dairy milk — only oat, soy, or almond.

requirementDefs.name: BaristaMinimumHours
requirementDefs.doc:
Staff members in the barista role must be
contracted for at least 12 hours per week.

constraintDefs.name: ConsentRecordedConstraint
constraintDefs.doc:
Evaluable rule: a valid consent record must exist
for the specified treatment before it can proceed.
At runtime, consentRecorded is derived from the
CDR: a consent composition exists for this patient
and treatment type with status 'given'.

constraintDefs.name: PatientInformationProvidedConstraint
constraintDefs.doc:
Evaluable rule: the patient must have been provided
with treatment information before consent is obtained.
At runtime, informationProvided is derived from the
CDR: an information-provision event is recorded for
this patient and treatment type, with a timestamp
before the consent timestamp.

constraintDefs.name: BaselineBloodsReviewedConstraint
constraintDefs.doc:
Evaluable rule: all required baseline blood tests
must have reached the 'reviewed' state before a
hormone therapy prescription can be authorised.
This checks two conditions:
1. All required tests have been performed (no

2. All results have been clinically reviewed (not

constraintDefs.name: ClinicalReviewCompletedConstraint
constraintDefs.doc:
Evaluable rule: a clinical review must have been
completed and documented before a prescribing
decision can proceed.
At runtime, reviewCompleted is derived from the
CDR: a consultation composition exists for this
episode with a review outcome recorded.

constraintDefs.name: RegimenWithinProtocolConstraint
constraintDefs.doc:
Evaluable rule: the proposed medication, route, and
dose must fall within the bounds of an approved
prescribing protocol.
At runtime, this evaluates the proposed regimen
against the protocol decision table in
Knowledge::DecisionModels. A regimen is within
protocol if all three components match an ap

constraintDefs.name: BloodMonitoringIntervalConstraint
constraintDefs.doc:
Evaluable rule: the number of weeks since the last
blood test must not exceed the required monitoring
interval.
At runtime, weeksSinceLastTest is derived from the
CDR: the most recent LabResult for this patient
with the relevant test name. requiredIntervalWeeks
comes from the prescribing protocol.

constraintDefs.name: DoseAdjustmentReviewedConstraint
constraintDefs.doc:
Evaluable rule: a clinical review must have been
completed, with current blood results reviewed,
before a dose adjustment can be authorised.
This is a compound check: both the clinical review
and the blood result review must be complete.

constraintDefs.name: SharedCareAcceptedConstraint
constraintDefs.doc:

the GP practice has confirmed acceptance of the

document has been sent.

constraintDefs.name: OrderSizeConstraint

quantity of items must be between 1 and 10.

if the drink is vegan, milk choice must not be dairy.

in compliance with COSHH requirements. Requires:

standards.

Testable condition: all staff who handle chemicals
have completed COSHH awareness training within the
required interval. Training must be refreshed
annually.

requirementInstances.name: coshhCompliance
requirementInstances.doc:
Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations 2002.
Requires employers to control substances that are hazardous
to health. For a laundry service: cleaning chemicals,
detergents, stain removers, and specialist products.
This exercises the governance traceability architecture
(A8) in a non-hea

attributes.name: regulatorySource
attributes.value: Health and Safety Executive — COSHH Regulations 2002

attributes.name: complianceDescription
attributes.value: All cleaning chemicals used in the laundry service must be subject to COSHH risk assessment. Current safety data sheets must be maintained for all substances. Staff must receive COSHH awareness training before handling chemicals. Chemicals must be stored in a ventilated, locked area with appropriate PPE available.

requirementInstances.name: animalWelfareDutyOfCare
requirementInstances.doc:
Animal Welfare Act 2006 — duty of care to animals
under your control. Applies to any person responsible
for an animal, including during grooming. Five welfare
needs: suitable environment, suitable diet, ability to
exhibit normal behaviour, housing with or apart from
other animals, protection from pa

attributes.value: Animal welfare duty of care during grooming

attributes.value: Public liability insurance, incident and observation log, first aid kit inspection records, groomer training and CPD records

Register of current Safety Data Sheets for every
chemical substance used. COSHH requires SDS to be
available at the point of use and kept current.

attributes.value: Index of all Safety Data Sheets held, with product name, supplier, date of issue, and location of physical/digital copy. Cross-referenced to chemical inventory.

Individual training records for each staff member

attributes.name: evidenceDescription
attributes.value: Per-employee record of COSHH awareness training: date completed, trainer, topics covered, competency assessment outcome. Refresher training tracked separately.

auditEvidenceInstances.name: storageInspectionLog
auditEvidenceInstances.doc:
Log of periodic inspections of the chemical storage
area. Checks ventilation, locked access, labelling,
PPE availability, and spill containment.

Styptic powder, bandages, antiseptic, eye wash,
emergency vet contact details.

CustomerSegment.name: CustomerSegment
CustomerSegment.doc:
A defined group of customers with shared needs,
behaviours, and willingness to pay. Each segment
has distinct needs and may require distinct value
propositions.

userFacing.shortDescription: A defined group of customers with shared needs and willingness to pay.

purposiveDescription.description: A group of people your service is designed for — people who share similar needs and reasons for choosing you. When you define your customer segments, the system uses them to connect your value propositions, pricing, and channels to the right audiences.

ValueProposition.name: ValueProposition
ValueProposition.doc:
A specific promise of value to a specific customer
segment. Defines what the customer gets, how it
differs from alternatives, and why it matters.

userFacing.shortDescription: A promise of value to a customer segment — what they get and why it matters.

purposiveDescription.description: The core promise your service makes to a particular group of customers — what they get from you and why they'd choose you over the alternatives. When you define a value proposition, the system holds it as the anchor that your activities, resources, and pricing all exist to deliver.

ServiceOffering.name: ServiceOffering
ServiceOffering.doc:
A packaged, deliverable unit of service that realises
one or more value propositions for one or more
segments. This is the unit at which pricing, resource
requirements, and pathway mapping are defined

userFacing.shortDescription: A packaged unit of service that can be priced, resourced, and delivered to customers.

purposiveDescription.description: A distinct service that your business offers — something a customer can choose, pay for, and receive. When you define a service offering, the system connects it to the activities required to deliver it, the resources it consumes, and the price the customer pays.

Channel.name: Channel
Channel.doc:
A means by which customers discover, access, and
interact with the service. Channels have reach,
cost, and conversion characteristics.

userFacing.shortDescription: A way that customers find, reach, or receive your service.

purposiveDescription.description: A way that customers find you, reach you, or receive your service — your website, a referral network, a walk-in counter, an app. When you define your channels, the system tracks which customer segments each channel serves and how your service offerings are delivered through them.

DifferentiationClaim.name: DifferentiationClaim
DifferentiationClaim.doc:
An explicit statement of how this service differs
from available alternatives, from the customer's
perspective. Each claim should be testable.

userFacing.shortDescription: An explicit, testable statement of how your service differs from alternatives.

purposiveDescription.description: An explicit statement of how your service differs from the alternatives, from the customer's perspective. Each claim should be testable — something you can back up with evidence. When you define differentiation claims, the system records them as commitments your service is designed to fulfil.

CatalogueEntry.name: CatalogueEntry
CatalogueEntry.doc:
The business decision to offer an item for sale or
use within a service. References an item definition
and adds business-context properties.
The four-layer model separates what something
intrinsically

userFacing.shortDescription: A record of something your business has decided to offer, with its price and status.

purposiveDescription.description: A record of something your business has decided to offer — whether that's a menu item, a treatment, a course, or any other unit you sell or provide. The catalogue entry connects what the thing intrinsically is to how your business offers it: its price, availability, and status. When you add a catalogue entry, the system tracks it as part of your active offering.

ExternalReference.name: ExternalReference
ExternalReference.doc:
A link to knowledge that lives outside the system.
The system does not own this data; it points to it.
Business meta model concept. Domain-agnostic:
  Coffee shop: supplier datasheet, origin cert
  He

userFacing.shortDescription: A link to authoritative knowledge that lives outside your system.

purposiveDescription.description: A link to knowledge that lives outside your system — a supplier datasheet, a regulatory standard, a clinical guideline, an accreditation body. The system doesn't own this information; it points to it, so you always know where authoritative external knowledge sits in relation to your service.

ActivityType.name: ActivityType
ActivityType.doc:
A defined type of activity within the business.
Every activity has a type, and every type belongs
to one of the five taxonomy categories.

userFacing.shortDescription: A defined kind of business activity, classified into one of five categories.

purposiveDescription.description: Something your business does — an identifiable unit of work that the system holds, tracks, and uses. In this system, every activity is an activity of one of the following types: service delivery, enabling, governance, development, or overhead. When you assign one of these types to an activity, the system will use that information to plan resources, allocate costs, and verify that governance requirements are being met for each kind of work.

weightedRelationships.rationale: Cost allocation is structurally determined by activity type — every cost line traces back to an activity category.
Granularity level directly governs how an activity type is tracked and costed — envelope vs category vs tracked.
Budgets aggregate by activity type but the relationship is indirect — mediated through cost allocation.
Activity records are typed by activity type but the record is an operational artefact, not a structural dependency.
Resources are consumed by activities but the mapping is many-to-many and context-dependent.
Channels deliver services which contain activities, but the relationship is distant — mediated through service offerings.

ActivityRecord.name: ActivityRecord
ActivityRecord.doc:
A recorded instance of an activity. At the tracked
level, the system produces these for every observable
activity. At coarser levels, they are estimated
aggregates.

userFacing.shortDescription: A recorded instance of an activity that actually happened.

purposiveDescription.description: A recorded instance of an activity that actually happened — the system's record that a specific piece of work was done, by whom, for how long, and using what resources. At the most detailed tracking level, the system creates one of these for every observable activity. At coarser levels, they are estimated aggregates.

ActivityBudget.name: ActivityBudget
ActivityBudget.doc:
A planned allocation of activity volume by type,
period, and resource. The activity-level equivalent
of a financial budget.

userFacing.shortDescription: A planned allocation of activity volume by type and period.

purposiveDescription.description: A planned allocation of how much activity of each type your business expects in a given period — the activity-level equivalent of a financial budget. When you define an activity budget, the system can compare what actually happened against what was planned, and surface gaps.

ActivityGranularity.name: ActivityGranularity
ActivityGranularity.doc:
Policy declaration: the granularity level at which
activity is tracked for a given business area.

userFacing.shortDescription: A policy declaration of how precisely activity is tracked in a given area.

purposiveDescription.description: A policy declaration: how precisely does your business track activity in a given area? The system supports three levels — envelope (a rough total), category (broken down by type), and tracked (every individual activity recorded). Different parts of your business can operate at different levels at the same time, and you can refine the level as your needs evolve.

ActivityCostAllocation.name: ActivityCostAllocation
ActivityCostAllocation.doc:
The mapping from an activity (or aggregate) to its
financial cost. Makes resource consumption visible
to the financial model.

userFacing.shortDescription: The mapping from an activity type to its financial cost.

purposiveDescription.description: The mapping from an activity to its financial cost — how much does it cost each time this kind of work is done? When you define cost allocations, the system can connect your activity model to your financial model, making resource consumption visible in financial terms.

ResourceType.name: ResourceType
ResourceType.doc:
A category of resource required to operate the
service delivery system. Each type has acquisition
characteristics, capacity constraints, and cost
profiles.

userFacing.shortDescription: A category of resource needed to run the service — people, equipment, premises, or external services.

purposiveDescription.description: A kind of thing your business needs in order to operate — staff, equipment, premises, technology, or external services such as a laboratory or a contractor. The system holds each resource type as a tracked concept. When you define your resource types, the system uses them to plan capacity, understand your cost base, and identify where you might be constrained.

ResourceInstance.name: ResourceInstance
ResourceInstance.doc:
A specific resource available to the business at
a defined capacity and cost. Represents planning-
level archetypes ("a prescribing clinician at
0.5 FTE") rather than named individuals.

userFacing.shortDescription: A specific resource available at a defined capacity and cost.

purposiveDescription.description: A specific resource available to your business at a defined capacity and cost — not a named individual, but a planning-level description like 'a prescribing clinician at 0.5 FTE' or 'one licensed copy of the booking system'. When you define resource instances, the system uses them to model your actual operating capacity.

Capability.name: Capability
Capability.doc:
An organised combination of resources that produces
a defined service function. Capabilities bridge the
gap between raw resources and service delivery — you
don't deliver care with "a doctor" and "a s

userFacing.shortDescription: An organised combination of resources that produces a defined service function.

purposiveDescription.description: An organised combination of resources that together produce a defined service function — like 'the ability to conduct a monitoring review' (which requires a clinician, a lab interface, and a clinical record system). You don't deliver services with individual resources; you deliver them with capabilities. When you define capabilities, the system connects your resources to the service offerings they enable.

CapacityModel.name: CapacityModel
CapacityModel.doc:
The relationship between resource configuration and
service throughput. A planning assertion, not a
computed formula — the formula representation lives
in BusinessScenarios::ProjectionFormula.
Capacit

userFacing.shortDescription: The relationship between your resource configuration and service throughput.

purposiveDescription.description: The relationship between your resource configuration and how much service you can deliver — for example, 'with one clinician at 0.5 FTE, we can support 20 active patients.' This is a planning assertion that the system holds, not a computed formula. When you define a capacity model, the system knows your throughput limits and can surface when you're approaching them.

ResourceConstraint.name: ResourceConstraint
ResourceConstraint.doc:
A constraint on resource availability or use that
affects service delivery. May be regulatory,
financial, temporal, or contractual.
Phase 7: regulatorySourceDescription retains the
human-readable refe

userFacing.shortDescription: A limit on resource availability that affects service delivery.

purposiveDescription.description: A limit on the availability or use of a resource that affects your ability to deliver services — regulatory, financial, temporal, or contractual. When you define resource constraints, the system tracks them alongside your resources so that capacity planning reflects real-world limits, not just theoretical availability.

InventoryRecord.name: InventoryRecord
InventoryRecord.doc:
A point-in-time record of stock level for an item
in the catalogue. References a catalogue entry
because inventory is scoped to what the business
currently offers.
Distinct from ResourceInstance (plan

userFacing.shortDescription: A point-in-time record of stock level for a catalogue item.

purposiveDescription.description: A point-in-time record of how much stock you have of something in your catalogue — how many tablets, how many bags of coffee beans, how many bottles of cleaning product. This is operational tracking: it tells the system what you have right now, so it can flag when you're running low. Distinct from resource planning, which is about strategic capacity.

ObjectiveCapabilityMapping.name: ObjectiveCapabilityMapping
ObjectiveCapabilityMapping.doc:
Maps a StrategicObjective to the Capability
usages that contribute to achieving it.
Phase 7 traceability pattern.

userFacing.shortDescription: A declared connection between a strategic objective and the capabilities that support it.

purposiveDescription.description: A declared connection between a strategic objective and the capabilities that contribute to achieving it. When you map objectives to capabilities, the system can trace from 'what are we trying to achieve?' down to 'what resources and service functions make that possible?' — closing the loop between strategy and operations.

RevenueStream.name: RevenueStream
RevenueStream.doc: A mechanism by which income is generated.

userFacing.shortDescription: A mechanism by which the business generates income from its services.

purposiveDescription.description: A way your business earns money — each revenue stream connects a customer segment, a triggering event (like completing an assessment or renewing a subscription), and a pricing model. When you define your revenue streams, the system can project income and connect it to the services that generate it.

CostDriver.name: CostDriver
CostDriver.doc: A structural factor that generates cost.

userFacing.shortDescription: A structural factor that generates cost in the business — linked to a resource or activity.

purposiveDescription.description: A structural factor that generates cost in your business — something that, as it scales or recurs, drives your expenditure. Each cost driver is linked to a resource or an activity. When you define your cost drivers, the system connects your cost structure to the resources and activities that produce it, so you can see where money goes and why.

UnitEconomics.name: UnitEconomics
UnitEconomics.doc: The financial profile of a single unit of service delivery.

userFacing.shortDescription: The revenue, cost, and margin for a single unit of service delivery.

purposiveDescription.description: The financial profile of delivering one unit of a service — what you earn, what it costs, and the margin between them. When you define unit economics for each service offering, the system can assess whether individual services are financially viable and how changes to pricing or costs would affect the picture.

PricingModel.name: PricingModel
PricingModel.doc: The logic that determines what a customer pays.

userFacing.shortDescription: How prices are set for services — per-episode, subscription, tiered, or other basis.

purposiveDescription.description: The logic that determines what a customer pays for a service — per-episode, subscription, tiered, sliding scale, or flat fee. When you define a pricing model, the system applies it to the relevant service offerings and uses it in revenue projections and unit economics calculations.

FinancialProjection.name: FinancialProjection
FinancialProjection.doc:
A named financial projection linked to a scenario.
Lightweight placeholder — full mechanics in
BusinessScenarios.

userFacing.shortDescription: A forward-looking financial picture combining revenues, costs, and growth assumptions.

purposiveDescription.description: A named projection of your business's financial future over a defined period — combining your revenue streams, cost drivers, and growth assumptions into a forward-looking picture. When you define a financial projection, the system links it to a scenario so you can compare different versions of the future side by side.

GovernanceRequirement.name: GovernanceRequirement
GovernanceRequirement.doc:
A regulatory, legal, or standards obligation that
the business must satisfy. General vocabulary —
applicable to COSHH, CQC, GDPR, food hygiene,
professional standards, or any regulatory context.
Domai

userFacing.shortDescription: A regulatory or standards obligation that the business must satisfy, with defined evidence.

purposiveDescription.description: A regulatory, legal, or standards obligation that your business must satisfy — and the system tracks it as a concrete, testable commitment, not just a policy statement. Each governance requirement is connected to the evidence that demonstrates compliance and, where formalised, to the constraint rules that the system can check. When you define governance requirements, the system builds a traceability chain from obligation through to proof.

AuditEvidenceRecord.name: AuditEvidenceRecord
AuditEvidenceRecord.doc:
A record or document that provides evidence of
compliance with a governance requirement. The
audit trail: what was checked, when, by whom,
and how often.
General vocabulary — applicable to any regulat

userFacing.shortDescription: A record that demonstrates compliance with a governance requirement — the proof that obligations are met.

purposiveDescription.description: A record that proves your business is meeting a governance requirement — what was checked, when, by whom, and how often. The system tracks these as concrete evidence items tied to specific obligations. When you define audit evidence records, the system knows what proof exists and can surface gaps where evidence is missing or overdue.

model variant. Selects which ServiceOfferings are

elements.name: row01
elements.doc:
Normal hormones, 12+ weeks, no significant
side effects, patient satisfied — stable.
Continue current regimen, standard monitoring.

elements.name: row02
elements.doc:
Normal hormones, 12+ weeks, no significant
side effects, patient neutral — stable but
explore satisfaction concerns. Continue
regimen with reduced monitoring interval.

elements.name: row03
elements.doc:
Normal hormones but less than 12 weeks on
treatment — too early to declare stable.
Continue and recheck.

elements.name: row04
elements.doc:
Low hormone levels — dose likely insufficient.
Adjust dose upward.

elements.name: row05
elements.doc:
High hormone levels — dose may need reducing.
Adjust dose downward.

elements.name: row06
elements.doc:
Normal hormones but warning-level side effects —
may need route or formulation change.
Increase monitoring, clinical review.

elements.name: row07
elements.doc:
Critical side effects regardless of hormone
levels — urgent clinical review.

elements.name: row08
elements.doc:
Suppressed hormone levels — possible over-
suppression. Urgent review to assess dose
and clinical status.

execution is derived from it.

and what the gap is. Self-knowledge is structural,
not bolt-on.

increasing patient autonomy and informed choice.

governance is a first-class system concern.
